task.title: Record a search that found nothing
task.shortdesc: Write down where you looked and what came back, so that you, or someone else, never has to look there again.

context.p: Write the search in a research note. This page records a search for the death of Charlotte Brontë in 1855, which found nothing under her own surname.

step.cmd: Open the form for a research note, as shows.
In , write where you looked, the name you used and what came back.

info.p: For example, Looked for her death in 1855 in an index of deaths, under the name Brontë. Nothing found. Looked again under Nicholls, her married name. Found: June quarter 1855, Keighley.

step.cmd: In , choose the status that fits.

info.p: If you will look again, choose .

step.cmd: Under , tie the note to Charlotte Brontë, the person you looked for.

info.p: Choose , then . Type Charlotte Brontë, choose the line with her years, 1816–1855, then choose .

result.p: Your note says where you looked, under what name, and what came back. A later reader can see the search and does not have to repeat it.
result.note: Good practice: not finding something tells you about the search. It does not tell you the person was not there.
